title: Like A Duck To Water
intro: What looks like giving up from outside feels like ownership from inside. The speaker accepts getting by, rejects other people's claims on him, and measures a good life by a small household and easy sleep. His independence is not absolute solitude: there is someone who loves him. Nor does the song completely separate contentment from resignation. The same position, day after day, can be a refuge precisely because nothing more is being demanded.
reading: Self-determined smallness, not total isolation; contentment retains a trace of resignation.

revisions.phrase-11-getting-by: The Chinese phrase often criticises someone for muddling through without ambition. He places it immediately after 'this is my life', taking ownership of an attitude other people might judge. The following claim to have walked his own road stops resignation from being the whole story. He is choosing the scale of the life, even if that choice does not resemble advancement. Keeping the phrase's faintly unflattering edge preserves this tension.
revisions.11-bowls: The refusal of spare place settings follows the statement that one woman loves him. The household is already enough; it is not empty. That distinction changes the apparent boast of needing nobody into a boundary around a particular intimacy. Critics and passing acquaintances do not automatically acquire a seat at this table. The image makes independence concrete without pretending that human attachment has ceased to matter.
revisions.phrase-11-knife: He stops the familiar saying before its promised instant Buddhahood. What follows is being in one's element and getting to sleep. The grand reward for laying down a weapon becomes an ordinary release from vigilance. Read in sequence, this is a withdrawal from conflict as much as a moral conversion: once he stops organising his life around other people's claims, rest becomes possible. The lyric does not identify an actual violent act being renounced.
revisions.11-pillow: An expression normally used for inseparable lovers transfers intimacy to the pillow. The joke is affectionate, but the surrounding same position, same days and same years also lets stasis show through. The song does not need to decide whether this routine is enviable or insufficient. Its argument is that the speaker gets to inhabit it on his own terms. The pillow offers attachment without the negotiations demanded by the people he excludes.
